full_judgment: "Mr. A.K. Badrul Huq, the learned Advocate appearing for the petitioners in both the petitions submits that though land of cadastral Survey Khatian Nos.18-21 had been shown as tenanted land in the sale deed dated 17.04.1926 under Cadastral Survey Khatian No.17 but the said under tenancies subsequently got no existence as under tenancies and the said land went to khan holding of Cadastral Survey Khatian No.17 and those land of under tenancies stood recorded in State Acquisition Khatian No.10 in the names of tenants or heirs of transferors Cadastral Survey Khatian No.17 and not in the names of heirs of any under tenants of Cadastral Survey Khatian Nos.18-21 and the deed of conveyance dated 17.04.1926 is a positive proof that Karim Uddin and his three (3) brothers purchased 3.76 acres of land from sons of Yakub Ali and Karim Uddin got. 94 acres of land in the case holding and pre-emptor-petitioner inherited .18-2 acres of land from his holding and father Karimuddin and pre-emptor petitioner still remains owner and co-sharer by way of inheritance in respect of li acres of land after transfer of .17 acres of land and pre-emptor petitioner having been a co sharer by way of inheritance, pre-emption cases by pre-emptor respondent is not at all maintain-able and both the trial Court and the Lower Appellate Court concurrently found that the pre-emptor petitioner is a co-sharer by inheritance and those findings rested upon correct construction and reading of the sale deed dated 17.04.1926, share of Yukub Ali in the case holding and materials on record but the learned Single Judge of the High Court Division totally misdirected himself in his approach in resolving the legal battle involved in pre-emption cases and committed a substantial error in holding that pre-emptor-petitioner inherited .13 acres of land and transferred .17 acres of land and thereby exhausted all his interest in case holding and became a stranger and this Division did not at all explore the legal controversy and in a summary way dismissed the leave petitions and judgment under challenge in Civil Review Petition may kindly be reviewed in the interest of justice.
